pulls.title: Add Setup Options for initial subscription flow control limits
pulls.author: afrind
pulls.body:
Addresses review feedback on PR #1 about subscriptions created by a PUBLISH that was not in response to SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.

* Add INITIAL_MAX_SUB_STREAMS (0x0C) and INITIAL_MAX_SUB_BYTES (0x0E) Setup Options. If omitted, the initial limit is 0.
* Both limits now always apply when the extension is negotiated. SUBSCRIBE or SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS can override an initial limit, including with a smaller value; PUBLISH echoes the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS value.
* Remove the rule that a limit absent at establishment does not apply, which contradicted the zero-credit default for PUBLISH.

pulls.title: Make an empty SUB_FLOW_CONTROL_UPDATE a protocol violation
pulls.author: afrind
pulls.body: Addresses review feedback on PR #1: a SUB_FLOW_CONTROL_UPDATE that carries neither MAX_SUB_STREAMS nor MAX_SUB_BYTES serves no purpose, so a publisher that receives one now closes the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION instead of ignoring it.

pulls.title: Clarify that credit updates are deltas and forbid a delta of 0
pulls.author: afrind
pulls.body:
Addresses review feedback on PR #1 asking whether limits must always increase. SUB_FLOW_CONTROL_UPDATE values were already added to the current limit; state that explicitly so limits never decrease.

As in HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE, a publisher that receives an update with a delta of 0 closes the session with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

pulls.title: Require reliable reset and add Stream Sequence to subgroup streams
pulls.author: afrind
pulls.body:
Addresses review feedback on PR #1 about correlating SUBGROUP_RESET with the reset stream. Group ID and Subgroup ID are not sufficient: a stream reset before its header arrives is unidentifiable, and a publisher can open more than one stream for the same subgroup.

* Endpoints offering the extension MUST support RESET_STREAM_AT, and publishers MUST reset subgroup streams with a reliable_size covering the SUBGROUP_HEADER.
* When the extension is negotiated, SUBGROUP_HEADER includes a per-subscription Stream Sequence. SUBGROUP_RESET identifies the stream by Stream Sequence instead of Group ID and Subgroup ID.
* A Stream Sequence at or above the stream limit is FLOW_CONTROL_EXCEEDED; a detected duplicate is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

pulls.title: Apply the Final Size check whenever the transport reports it
pulls.author: afrind
pulls.body:
Addresses review feedback on PR #1 about WebTransport and the Final Size cross-check. WebTransport implementations do not necessarily expose a reset stream's final size; when the transport does report it, a mismatch with SUBGROUP_RESET is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

* Drop the FIN case, which never produces a SUBGROUP_RESET to check.
* Trim the Security Considerations paragraph to describe the threat and point to Byte Accounting instead of restating the rule.
